labeler: blind independent review, generic OWASP rubric, no knowledge of the tool under test

labels.note: The admin gate for /api/admin/* and /admin/dashboard splits the admin_session cookie on '.', decodes only the base64 payload (line 27-30) and trusts payload.role/exp (line 31) WITHOUT ever recomputing/verifying the HMAC signature that login attaches (app/api/admin/login/route.ts lines 14-18). An attacker can forge admin_session = base64({"role":"admin","exp":<future>}) + '.x' and pass the check. The admin route handlers (app/api/admin/users, .../scores) do no further auth, so this bypass dumps every user's id/name/email/username (users/route.ts) and all scores -- authentication bypass / broken access control.

supabaseServiceKey is read from process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY (line 5) and used to build the RLS-bypassing supabaseAdmin client (createClient, line 18). The NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix inlines the key into client bundles, and app/dashboard/all-prompts/page.tsx is a 'use client' page (line 1) that imports supabaseAdmin (line 4) and calls it in the browser -- including supabaseAdmin.from('prompts').delete().eq('id', deletePromptId) at line 92 -- so the full-admin key ships to every visitor and the browser performs privileged, RLS-bypassing reads/deletes.

The admin-token signing secret falls back to a committed hard-coded string 'promptos-admin-fallback-secret' when NEXTAUTH_SECRET is unset (line 6); anyone reading the repo can mint validly-signed admin tokens (independent of the L1 verification gap).

notes: Provenance: Yuvadi29/PromptOS, a real public Next.js (App Router) + Supabase prompt-engineering app (recall case; NOT authored by us). Three distinct issues: (L1) the admin auth middleware never verifies the HMAC signature it issues, so the admin_session cookie is forgeable and all /api/admin/* endpoints (incl. an all-users PII dump) are reachable unauthenticated; (L2) the Supabase service_role key is exposed via NEXT_PUBLIC_ and the admin client is imported+used inside a 'use client' page, shipping RLS-bypass to the browser; (L3) a hard-coded fallback signing secret. Deliberate non-findings verified: the non-admin mutating routes I inspected (app/api/feedback/route.ts, app/api/save-prompt/route.ts) DO enforce getServerSession(authOptions) and return 401 when unauthenticated -- correctly authenticated, not flagged; NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY (lib/supabase.ts line 4) is public by design and not flagged; the admin_session cookie is set httpOnly/sameSite=lax and secure-in-prod (login route 44-50), so no insecure-cookie label.
